source.filename: frontiers-Soft Manipulators and Grippers- A Review-2016.pdf

actuation: pneumatic actuation (McKibben artificial muscles, fluidic elastomer actuators / FEA, PneuFlex, Pneumatic Networks / Pneu-Nets, chemical pressure generation, combustion)
constitutive_assumptions: Materials used in soft robotics exhibit Young's modulus comparable to soft biological tissues (~1 GPa or lower) with non-linear, hyperelastic behavior.
Rigid body modeling assumptions (rigid links between components) are inapplicable to continuum soft bodies.
Kinematic models frequently assume constant curvature across continuum sections, though non-constant curvature models account for distributed weight, payloads, and inherent torsion.
Actuation cables possess high longitudinal tensile strength with negligible strain/elongation along their axis, bending freely in other directions without volume change.

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Soft manipulator design operates within a 2D qualitative design space characterized by trade-offs between precision and degrees of freedom, and between structural compliance and force exertion.

3D printing enables the fabrication of complex, amorphous geometries and embedded microfluidic channels or logic, but printable soft materials are relatively brittle compared to molded elastomers and less suited for high-pressure actuation.

Modeling continuum soft manipulators requires methods beyond rigid-body kinematics, including constant curvature approximations, Jacobian methods, feed-forward neural networks, real-time finite element modeling (FEM), and discrete voxel mass-spring lattice simulators.
Variable stiffness can be implemented in soft manipulators via particle jamming (locking granular media under vacuum) or through adjustable stiffness layers integrated into pneumatic actuators.
evidence_relevant_to_topic.evidence_type: literature review of variable stiffness mechanisms

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Passive underactuated soft grippers made of compliant materials such as hot melt adhesive can achieve force and form closure purely through structural deformation and contact interaction forces without active motors.

Soft sensing faces substantial challenges because infinite degrees of freedom preclude one-to-one sensor-to-DOF mapping, wiring connections risk impeding robot compliance, and ionic resistive sensors struggle to isolate strain from pressure without multi-layered architectures.

experimental_setup: Review paper: evaluates benchmarking tasks from the RoboSoft Grand Challenge manipulation competition (locating, grasping, and boxing delicate to heavy/awkward objects; navigating an arm through rigid obstacles/cylinders; opening a door via a handle).

Surveys literature experimental setups, including pneumatic pressure testing benches, tensile/dynamic strain testing of sensors, and robotic arm push-grasping tests of passive hot melt adhesive grippers.
future_work: Overcoming trade-offs in speed, precision, repeatability, and grasping force through advances in materials, morphology, actuation, and sensors.
Developing soft sensors capable of undergoing large deformations that allow localized tactile and posture sensing while decoupling pressure and strain.
Improving physical wiring and manufacturing integration of sensors into continuum manipulators without compromising structural compliance.
Establishing closed-loop tactile feedback control for soft manipulators interacting with uncertain and dynamic surroundings.
Deploying compliant soft manipulators in industrial automation, agricultural processing, and safe human-robot interaction environments.
limitations_inferred: As a qualitative review paper, no primary empirical bench tests or quantitative comparative datasets were generated across the surveyed mechanisms.
The proposed four-axis design space trade-offs are presented qualitatively without formal mathematical models or validated bounds.

Long-term fatigue, cyclic creep, thermal dissipation (specifically for shape memory alloys), and environmental degradation of soft polymers are discussed conceptually rather than comprehensively quantified.
limitations_stated_by_authors: Soft manipulators inherently suffer from lower grasping force, lower precision, and a lack of repeatability compared to rigid robots.
High or infinite degrees of freedom make precise kinematic control and modeling challenging and computationally intensive.
Soft materials present challenges regarding non-linear responses, difficulty in simulation and modeling, requirements for self-repair, fatigue failure, and fabrication limits.
Layered casting and soft lithography methods tend to constrain robot morphology to planar shapes rather than fully amorphous 3D geometries.
3D-printed flexible materials remain relatively brittle compared to molded silicone rubbers, restricting their utility in pressurized actuation.
Cable-driven actuation requires external rotary or linear actuation sources, which can make systems bulky.

Soft sensing lacks one-to-one pairing of sensor to degree of freedom; ionic sensors cannot decouple strain and pressure without specialized multi-layer designs; flexible electronics withstand only minimal strain; and optical tactile sensors require rigid cameras positioned close to the deformation zone.
Physical connections (electrodes, wires) to soft sensors can restrict the compliance and dynamic behavior of soft robotic systems.
Scientific progress in understanding and fabricating soft manipulators trails behind the demands and aspirations of practical applications.
main_results: Soft robotics exploits material compliance and deformability to achieve structural adaptation and safe physical interaction in unstructured environments.
Manipulator capabilities are governed by intrinsic design trade-offs: higher degrees of freedom decrease precision control, and higher structural compliance reduces maximum force exertion.

Fabrication relies on casting/molding, shape deposition manufacturing (SDM), soft lithography, and additive manufacturing (3D/4D printing), each balancing geometric complexity against material durability and pressure tolerance.
Primary actuation strategies encompass pneumatic networks/FEA, cable/tendon drives, shape memory alloys, electroactive polymers/dielectric elastomers, and passive underactuated mechanisms.
Stiffness modulation can be realized morphologically through vacuum-driven particle jamming or pneumatic adjustable stiffness layers.

Soft sensing technologies (resistive ionic channels, flexible organic transistors, piezoelectric/capacitive elements, conductive thermoplastics, and optical methods) offer deformation detection but face significant integration and decoupling challenges.
modeling_methods: Jacobian methods for tendon-driven continuum manipulators
feed-forward neural network learning for inverse kinetics
Finite Element Modeling (FEM), including real-time FEM for control
non-linear relaxation kinematic simulation using spring-beam-mass systems
geometrically exact models accounting for non-linearities and distributed payloads
performance_metrics: maximum strain (e.g., 100% to 300% in soft sensors)
sensor stability over time and sensitivity
possible_gap_implications: The trade-off between compliance and force exertion indicates that purely soft manipulators may require variable stiffness mechanisms (e.g., particle jamming, layer jamming) or rigid-soft hybrid backbones to perform high-load industrial manipulation without sacrificing delicate compliance.

The inability to map individual sensors to individual DOFs in infinite-DOF continuum bodies implies that future control schemes will need to leverage embodied intelligence, dense sensor skin arrays, or learning-based state estimators rather than traditional analytical inverse kinematics.

The reported brittleness of 3D-printed elastomers compared to molded silicone implies a materials science gap in fatigue-resistant, highly stretchable additive manufacturing resins for pneumatic soft robotics.
paper.research_objective: To review and assess the current state of the art in soft manipulators and grippers, evaluating materials, fabrication methods, actuation strategies, morphology, and soft sensing technologies, while analyzing achievements, shortcomings, and potential impacts on industry and society.
paper.research_problem: Conventional rigid robotic systems rely on rigid links, fixed joints, and low mechanical flexibility, making them ill-suited for safe operation and adaptation in unstructured, dynamic, and poorly defined human environments; furthermore, they struggle to combine delicate, compliant manipulation with significant force transmission.
stiffness_mechanism: intrinsic material compliance (elastomers, silicones, hot melt adhesives)
paper.title: Soft Manipulators and Grippers: A Review
